newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields creep higher at close in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields creep higher at close in thin trade.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ bond yields continue to creep higher at close
* Friday's Labour Cost Index data the next focus
New Zealand yields continued to creep higher at Tuesday's close in the absence of any real information to trade off.
It was a quiet day in terms of domestic news, and the usual guidance taken from U.S. Treasuries was diminished by a President's Day holiday on Monday.

Local bonds stayed on the weaker path they opened on, nudging a couple of basis points higher in yield. Maturities in the mid part of the curve ended four basis points weaker at 7.26 percent while the long bond was off three at 7.29 percent.
Volumes were moderate in the short end of the futures market, with 1,656 March contracts traded to finish four basis points weaker at 92.56.
The physical 90-day bank bills closed three basis points higher at 7.40 percent, and dealers said the session had been nothing to write home about.

Rates had the potential to move lower if the currency could be sustained over US$0.69, but the market was searching for a trigger, they said. Friday's Labour cost data is the next local news on the agenda.
